newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM seeks to step up China ties with visit.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM seeks to step up China ties with visit.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh visits China this week to cement ties between the armed forces of the two nations and boost economic relations, analysts said on Monday.

During his April 2-5 visit to Beijing, he will use his close personal relationships with senior Chinese leaders to seek greater security for Thai investments both in Hong Hong and on the Chinese mainland, the analysts told Reuters.
Chavalit will be accompanied by a 120-member delegation that will include the Thai armed forces chief and senior businessmen.

"The Chinese government has given us a great honour by scheduling the Thai premier to meet four of the supreme leaders of the seven-member politburo of the Communist Party," a government statement said.
Chavalit is to meet President Jiang Zemin, Prime Minister Li Peng, deputy premier Zhu Rongji, and the vice chairman of the Chinese central military commission, Liu Huaquing, it said.

"The visit is to strengthen bilateral relations, to set guidelines for economic cooperation, exchange views on the international political situation and stabilisation, and seek a partnership for mutual interest," it said.
In the 1980's when he was Thai army commander, Chavalit began buying weapons from China, analysts noted. Previously, the military had bought most of its weaponry from the United States.

"Militarily, it was widely known that Chavalit was the one who shifted from Western dominated weapons to Chinese weapons 10 years ago, and he has personal relationships with Chinese leaders," said Prathumporn Watcharasatheira, a lecturer in international relations at Chulalongkorn University.
Chavalit's ties with Chinese leaders date back to the 1980's when as aide to then Prime Minister Prem Tinasulanonda, he led several military delegations to China over nearly a decade.
He has also made a series of visits to Beijing as Thailand's defence minister over the last three years.
"Li Peng and others Chinese leaders are our close friends, our brothers," Chavalit told reporters recently.
Thailand is also one of the biggest Asian investors in China and it has special relations with Beijing through the private sector, said Prathumporn.
Among the biggest Thai investors is the Charoen Pokphand group, which is involved in multi-billion dollar agri-business and auto parts making in China .
Thai paper and pulp firm, Advance Agro Holding Plc, has plans to jointly invest 27 billion baht ($1.04 billion) with the Chinese government in a pulp plant in Thailand.
Commerce ministry officials said Thailand hopes to complete deals to sell rice, rubber and tapioca starch this year to China, which has a huge consumer base with strong demand.

Expectations were that agreements could be reached to sell as much as 700,000 tonnes of rice, 400,000 tonnes of rubber and 100,000 tonnes of tapioca starch to China this year, a senior ministry official said.
